Research how shoppers with this persona's characteristics discover, evaluate, compare and buy products in those two retail environments.

Method:
- Use web search. Look for Sephora- and Ulta-specific evidence first: the retailers' own help, policy and feature pages, investor and press materials, retail trade press, and consumer research that names these retailers. Then general US beauty retail research where retailer-specific evidence is missing.
- Mark every point as **[Retailer-specific]** (a cited source is specifically about Sephora or Ulta), **[General beauty retail]** (cited, but not retailer-specific) or **[Inference]** (a reasoned translation of the persona's traits, no direct source).
- Site features: list only features you can document with a cited source (for example review filters, loyalty programs, new or trending sections, try-on tools). If a feature cannot be verified, do not list it as existing.
- Never invent statistics, studies, features or URLs. If evidence is missing, say so.
- Cite every factual claim inline as a Markdown link to the exact page you used, in the form ([page title](page URL)). Only link pages that appeared in your search results.
- Describe behavior, not demographics.

content.text:
## 1. Sephora: site features and shopping tools
- **[Retailer-specific]** Ratings & Reviews system to voice opinions about recent beauty buys, requiring registration before rating and writing reviews ([Customer Service - Ratings & Reviews | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Free Beauty Insider loyalty program that lets members earn points on merchandise purchases and redeem points for rewards ([About Beauty Insider Loyalty Program | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Two free samples with every online merchandise order, selectable via Beauty Offers / Basket ([Customer Service: Samples & Promotions | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Trending Products page framing trending items as products taking social media by storm ([Trending Products | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Virtual Artist AR try-on for makeup, developed with ModiFace using facial tracking to digitally test products ([How Sephora Uses AI: 10 Real AI Case Studies with Results, Scale & Strategy [2026]](https://digitaldefynd.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Beauty Insider Community forums where members share reviews, tips, tutorials and product recommendations ([Home - Beauty Insider Community](https://community.sephora.com)).

## 2. Ulta Beauty: site features and shopping tools
- **[Retailer-specific]** Product pages with Ratings & Reviews plus Q&A, showing recommend-to-friend percentage and helpful reviews ([Good Molecules - Hydrating Facial Cleansing Gel | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Free Ultamate Rewards program where members earn points on purchases and redeem points for discounts and products ([Ulta Beauty Rewards: Digital Transformation and Loyalty](https://myhubble.money)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** GLAMlab virtual try-on in the app to try thousands of products including lipstick, eyeliner, foundation and eyeshadow before buying ([How Ulta Beauty is giving omnichannel retail a fresh face | Google Cloud Blog](https://cloud.google.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** New Arrivals, Bestsellers / Most-loved favorites and Trending now merchandising groupings ([New Beauty Products | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Conscious Beauty program with Clean Ingredients, Cruelty Free, Vegan and Sustainable Packaging badges to identify qualifying brands and products ([Conscious Beauty | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Gifts With Purchase and bonus offers, including brand-specific deluxe samples and tiered beauty bags with qualifying shipped purchases ([Does Ulta Beauty Give Samples?](https://gbtimes.com)).

## 3. Retailer-specific evidence on how shoppers discover, evaluate and buy
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora has built its own social virality, but virality still ends in a separate step where a shopper sees the trend on social media then visits Sephora's site or store to buy ([TikTok Shop Closes in on Sephora in US Online Beauty, while Amazon and Walmart Stay on Top](https://ecdb.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora will launch on TikTok Shop in the US with Sephora Drop Shop, a monthly program centered on exclusive product launches, creator content and TikTok LIVE events ([How Sephora’s TikTok Shop Strategy Is Turning Social Discovery into Commerce](https://beautymatter.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Ulta became the first retailer in the beauty category to launch a TikTok Shop and partners with macro influencers plus store associates posting content ([Why Ulta Beauty thinks AI makes the store experience matter more](https://thedrum.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Daily TikTok users who discover products via influencers show elevated shopping at Ulta Beauty at 25% versus 13% comparison ([TikTok made me buy it: Who’s discovering new products on social media in 2026?](https://yougov.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** 58% of online shoppers prefer to begin the search for beauty products on a beauty retailer's website such as Ulta.com or Sephora.com ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** 92% of consumers say reviews are a factor when considering a new beauty product never purchased before ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).

## 4. How this persona's traits show up at Sephora
- **[Inference]** High trend_sensitivity (0.90) and novelty_seeking (0.85) direct attention first to Trending Products and new-launch entry points, then to external validation before deciding.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Need for shade and ingredient clarity maps to Ratings & Reviews details and Clean at Sephora ingredient positioning, since Clean at Sephora signals formulated-without standards ([Customer Service - Ratings & Reviews | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Inference]** Medium influencer_trust (0.60) plus high research_depth (0.70) means creator demonstration is treated as a candidate trigger, not proof, with corroboration sought in review volume, recent sentiment and tutorials.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Preference for interactive try-on or timely promotion maps to Virtual Artist for visual shade proof and Beauty Insider points plus samples that lower trial risk for trending items ([How Sephora Uses AI: 10 Real AI Case Studies with Results, Scale & Strategy [2026]](https://digitaldefynd.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Rejection of items with poor effectiveness signals or lack of recent reviews aligns with evidence that review volume and recency drive efficacy judgments, with 58% caring about volume and 49% referring to recent reviews ([Stat: Inter-Covid beauty purchases rely on reviews](https://lsnglobal.com)).
- **[Inference]** Medium price_sensitivity (0.65) allows tolerating higher prices for highly desirable viral items, but only when effectiveness signals and promotion or value justification are present.

## 5. How this persona's traits show up at Ulta Beauty
- **[Inference]** Broad comparison behavior maps to moving across Ulta's New Arrivals, Trending now, Bestsellers and Only at Ulta assortments to build a consideration set rather than buying on first exposure.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Verification of shade, usage and claims maps to GLAMlab Foundation Shade Matcher and shade swatching plus Q&A on product pages before purchase ([How Ulta Beauty is giving omnichannel retail a fresh face | Google Cloud Blog](https://cloud.google.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Reliance on ratings and recent review volume aligns with findings that 88% of beauty shoppers consider ratings and reviews before buying ([Latest Beauty Ecommerce SEO Statistics](https://seosandwitch.com)).
- **[Inference]** Creator or peer demonstration naming the exact item triggers a switch to search and marketplace listings to verify item name, price, effectiveness and reviews, consistent with Ulta's strong visibility in general and AI-assisted product search.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Promotion sensitivity maps to Ultamate Rewards points, weekly ads, gifts with purchase and Conscious Beauty badges that add value or ingredient reassurance without abandoning trend appeal ([Conscious Beauty | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com)).
- **[Inference]** If shade, ingredient or usage information cannot be verified, the persona defers purchase and continues browsing alternatives rather than impulse-checking out.

## 6. Sephora versus Ulta Beauty for this persona
- **[Inference]** Sephora functions more as trend-validation and prestige-newness hub, while Ulta functions more as breadth-comparison and value-validation hub across prestige, mass and exclusives.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora offers Trending Products positioned explicitly around social media virality, whereas Ulta merchandises Trending now alongside Most-loved favorites and Only at Ulta exclusives ([Trending Products | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Both offer AR try-on, but via different tools: Sephora Virtual Artist versus Ulta GLAMlab with Foundation Shade Matcher ([How Ulta Beauty is giving omnichannel retail a fresh face | Google Cloud Blog](https://cloud.google.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Both benefit from the same journey split where social inspires but retailer sites close the sale: 38% recalled seeing a new beauty product on social media that they later purchased, rising to 62% for Gen Z ([TikTok vs Google for Beauty Discovery: When to Use Each](https://umatechnology.org)).
- **[Inference]** Ulta's wider price ladder and frequent gifts with purchase better satisfy the persona's price-versus-effectiveness check for unproven viral items; Sephora's samples-plus-Rewards Bazaar better support low-risk trial of prestige launches.
- **[Inference]** Neither retailer alone replaces social discovery and video tutorials; the persona will still start on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube and use both retailer sites primarily for verification and fulfillment.

## 7. Evidence quality and gaps
- **[Retailer-specific]** Strong evidence for loyalty programs, samples, trending / new-arrival merchandising, try-on tools and community from retailer help pages and established tech press ([About Beauty Insider Loyalty Program | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Strong survey evidence for review dependence and retailer-site-first research, but samples are from PowerReviews-tracked beauty shoppers and may not equal the trend-driven subsegment ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Social discovery evidence is robust directionally across Tinuiti, YouGov and Stella Rising summaries, but platform shares vary by survey year, question wording and age cut ([57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search](https://searchengineland.com)).
- **[Inference]** No verified retailer-specific source was found in search results detailing on-site review filter options, shade-finder accuracy, or conversion impact of samples for trend shoppers; those mechanics should not be assumed.
- **[Inference]** No verified statistic was found in search results isolating this exact persona's tolerance for higher prices or mixed reviews; price-tolerance claims remain hypotheses from the provided parameters.
- **[Inference]** TikTok Shop launch timing and assortment details for Sephora and Ulta are evolving and reported via trade press; checkout behavior may shift from separate-step validation toward in-app purchase as these storefronts mature.

- **[Retailer-specific]** Beauty Insider Community forums where members share reviews, tips, tutorials and product recommendations ([Home - Beauty Insider Community](https://community.sephora.com)).

## 3. Retailer-specific evidence on how shoppers discover, evaluate and buy
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora has built its own social virality, but virality still ends in a separate step where a shopper sees the trend on social media then visits Sephora's site or store to buy ([TikTok Shop Closes in on Sephora in US Online Beauty, while Amazon and Walmart Stay on Top](https://ecdb.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora will launch on TikTok Shop in the US with Sephora Drop Shop, a monthly program centered on exclusive product launches, creator content and TikTok LIVE events ([How Sephora’s TikTok Shop Strategy Is Turning Social Discovery into Commerce](https://beautymatter.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Ulta became the first retailer in the beauty category to launch a TikTok Shop and partners with macro influencers plus store associates posting content ([Why Ulta Beauty thinks AI makes the store experience matter more](https://thedrum.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Daily TikTok users who discover products via influencers show elevated shopping at Ulta Beauty at 25% versus 13% comparison ([TikTok made me buy it: Who’s discovering new products on social media in 2026?](https://yougov.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** 58% of online shoppers prefer to begin the search for beauty products on a beauty retailer's website such as Ulta.com or Sephora.com ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** 92% of consumers say reviews are a factor when considering a new beauty product never purchased before ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).

## 4. How this persona's traits show up at Sephora
- **[Inference]** High trend_sensitivity (0.90) and novelty_seeking (0.85) direct attention first to Trending Products and new-launch entry points, then to external validation before deciding.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Need for shade and ingredient clarity maps to Ratings & Reviews details and Clean at Sephora ingredient positioning, since Clean at Sephora signals formulated-without standards ([Customer Service - Ratings & Reviews | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Inference]** Medium influencer_trust (0.60) plus high research_depth (0.70) means creator demonstration is treated as a candidate trigger, not proof, with corroboration sought in review volume, recent sentiment and tutorials.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Preference for interactive try-on or timely promotion maps to Virtual Artist for visual shade proof and Beauty Insider points plus samples that lower trial risk for trending items ([How Sephora Uses AI: 10 Real AI Case Studies with Results, Scale & Strategy [2026]](https://digitaldefynd.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Rejection of items with poor effectiveness signals or lack of recent reviews aligns with evidence that review volume and recency drive efficacy judgments, with 58% caring about volume and 49% referring to recent reviews ([Stat: Inter-Covid beauty purchases rely on reviews](https://lsnglobal.com)).
- **[Inference]** Medium price_sensitivity (0.65) allows tolerating higher prices for highly desirable viral items, but only when effectiveness signals and promotion or value justification are present.

## 5. How this persona's traits show up at Ulta Beauty
- **[Inference]** Broad comparison behavior maps to moving across Ulta's New Arrivals, Trending now, Bestsellers and Only at Ulta assortments to build a consideration set rather than buying on first exposure.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Verification of shade, usage and claims maps to GLAMlab Foundation Shade Matcher and shade swatching plus Q&A on product pages before purchase ([How Ulta Beauty is giving omnichannel retail a fresh face | Google Cloud Blog](https://cloud.google.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Reliance on ratings and recent review volume aligns with findings that 88% of beauty shoppers consider ratings and reviews before buying ([Latest Beauty Ecommerce SEO Statistics](https://seosandwitch.com)).
- **[Inference]** Creator or peer demonstration naming the exact item triggers a switch to search and marketplace listings to verify item name, price, effectiveness and reviews, consistent with Ulta's strong visibility in general and AI-assisted product search.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Promotion sensitivity maps to Ultamate Rewards points, weekly ads, gifts with purchase and Conscious Beauty badges that add value or ingredient reassurance without abandoning trend appeal ([Conscious Beauty | Ulta Beauty](https://www.ulta.com)).
- **[Inference]** If shade, ingredient or usage information cannot be verified, the persona defers purchase and continues browsing alternatives rather than impulse-checking out.

## 6. Sephora versus Ulta Beauty for this persona
- **[Inference]** Sephora functions more as trend-validation and prestige-newness hub, while Ulta functions more as breadth-comparison and value-validation hub across prestige, mass and exclusives.
- **[Retailer-specific]** Sephora offers Trending Products positioned explicitly around social media virality, whereas Ulta merchandises Trending now alongside Most-loved favorites and Only at Ulta exclusives ([Trending Products | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[Retailer-specific]** Both offer AR try-on, but via different tools: Sephora Virtual Artist versus Ulta GLAMlab with Foundation Shade Matcher ([How Ulta Beauty is giving omnichannel retail a fresh face | Google Cloud Blog](https://cloud.google.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Both benefit from the same journey split where social inspires but retailer sites close the sale: 38% recalled seeing a new beauty product on social media that they later purchased, rising to 62% for Gen Z ([TikTok vs Google for Beauty Discovery: When to Use Each](https://umatechnology.org)).
- **[Inference]** Ulta's wider price ladder and frequent gifts with purchase better satisfy the persona's price-versus-effectiveness check for unproven viral items; Sephora's samples-plus-Rewards Bazaar better support low-risk trial of prestige launches.
- **[Inference]** Neither retailer alone replaces social discovery and video tutorials; the persona will still start on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube and use both retailer sites primarily for verification and fulfillment.

## 7. Evidence quality and gaps
- **[Retailer-specific]** Strong evidence for loyalty programs, samples, trending / new-arrival merchandising, try-on tools and community from retailer help pages and established tech press ([About Beauty Insider Loyalty Program | Sephora](https://www.sephora.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Strong survey evidence for review dependence and retailer-site-first research, but samples are from PowerReviews-tracked beauty shoppers and may not equal the trend-driven subsegment ([Meeting Beauty Shopper Digital Expectations in a Post-Pandemic World](https://powerreviews.com)).
- **[General beauty retail]** Social discovery evidence is robust directionally across Tinuiti, YouGov and Stella Rising summaries, but platform shares vary by survey year, question wording and age cut ([57% of beauty consumers don’t start with Google Search](https://searchengineland.com)).
- **[Inference]** No verified retailer-specific source was found in search results detailing on-site review filter options, shade-finder accuracy, or conversion impact of samples for trend shoppers; those mechanics should not be assumed.
- **[Inference]** No verified statistic was found in search results isolating this exact persona's tolerance for higher prices or mixed reviews; price-tolerance claims remain hypotheses from the provided parameters.
- **[Inference]** TikTok Shop launch timing and assortment details for Sephora and Ulta are evolving and reported via trade press; checkout behavior may shift from separate-step validation toward in-app purchase as these storefronts mature.
